documents.text: Persistent foamy urine can warrant urinalysis and clinical evaluation. A symptom alone does not establish proteinuria.
Breathing difficulty with severe symptoms requires urgent in-person assessment.
Headache assessment considers onset and neurological warning signs.
Fever guidance depends on age, duration and associated symptoms.
Medication guidance should consider dose, allergies and interactions.
Skin complaints require description of onset, distribution and severity.
Pregnancy can change which treatments and investigations are appropriate.
Children may require age-specific assessment and dosing.
